Unit 1 · Foundations of Creativity and Innovation · 120 minutes · studio · COs 109.1, 109.2

slides.speaker_notes: Studio session. Warm-up: 30 Circles. Do not lecture past 15 minutes.

slides.title: The one idea

content_blocks.block_data: The good idea is not the hard part. The hard part is everything that happens after it.

slides.speaker_notes: Say it once. Do not elaborate on the slide — elaborate out loud.

slides.title: Why it matters

block_data.body: Preparation, incubation, illumination, verification, implementation. Illumination is the one everybody romanticises and the one that takes the least time.
The idea that arrives in the bus is paid for by the two hours you spent stuck the day before.

slides.speaker_notes: Four beats across two slides. Fifteen minutes for all of it.

slides.title: What to do with it

block_data.body: Two gaps: between illumination and verification (no cheap way to test), and between verification and implementation (it works, nobody does it).
Your anchor's owner is stuck at exactly one of these stages. Naming which one is today's work.

slides.speaker_notes: Four beats across two slides. Fifteen minutes for all of it.

slides.title: Today you will

content_blocks.block_data: Find out which stage your anchor's owner is stuck at, and write the problem in one sentence you could act on.

slides.speaker_notes: Leave this slide up for the whole making phase.

slides.title: To close

block_data.head: Pitch
block_data.body: Three minutes. The person, the stuck, the idea, the picture, the ask.

block_data.head: Critique
block_data.body: I like… / I wish… / What if… — the idea, never the person.

block_data.head: Idea log
block_data.body: One page. Silent. Box 4 is the one you read again in week 15.

slides.speaker_notes: If time runs short, cut the input — never the pitch. The pitch is how CO 109.2 is attained.
